purpose: Requirement-derived native-only expected case inventory for #2753. This is data, not executable tests or a prompt-runtime scenario. Actual public module operations use scratch Git/HOME, real native ordinary-record storage and injected external effects; no real agents, providers or staging. The production synchronous updateRun callback is a real native function, not a JSON string adapter. Native filesystem ownership and actual worker overlap are unbound to the Interpreter. Dollar-prefixed values reference fixture-owned identities. Each variants row expands into independent cases. Independent preservation and intentional-effect assertions must run separately, so an earlier failure cannot hide controls. No ordering of competing same-field intentions is newly specified.

criteria.text: When an earlier status refresh, step completion or question command saves after newer unrelated work was recorded, that newer work remains saved, including completed steps, questions, gates, decisions, area progress and PR fields.
When two overlapping commands successfully record different unrelated steps, both steps remain saved; sequential completions retain both steps too.
Running a completed step again still clears later known steps of its own area, including a later step added or replaced while the command was running; unrelated steps remain saved.
Asking a question saves that requested question, and refreshing status saves the actual refreshed CI result, while each command retains unrelated newer progress.
Ordinary progress saves leave accepted change requests, delivery state and acknowledgement time and note unchanged; existing warning-only uptake visibility and approval rules still apply.
A command selected for an older run cannot change a replacement run at the same location, and a failed progress save ends with a clear failure rather than claiming it was saved.
